solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Problem with sheep neck mostly used with pastry dish

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: scrag is the bony neck of mutton
a pie is a dish baked in pastry

explanation.surface: A cook complains about a sheep's neck being stuffed into a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims SCRAG to SCRA. Scrapie is a fatal brain disease of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a degenerative disease affecting sheep, so it is literally a problem for the flock.

clue.text: Support traveller who may not get on flight

definitions.text: traveller who may not get on flight
definitions.meaning: a passenger without a confirmed seat, waiting for a spare place

explanation.surface: Backing for a passenger who might be left at the airport.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means remain loyal to; the noun is an unconfirmed air passenger waiting for a seat.

clue.text: Reward rebel in revolt, one hiding in the marshes

indicators.note: a rebel in revolt is up in arms, turned over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel paid off during an uprising goes to ground in the marshes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolt' rearranges REWARD REBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird that nests among reeds, often heard rather than seen in wetland.

clue.text: Rod keeps sex-appeal cultivated

indicators.note: the rod keeps, or holds, the other piece inside it

parts.note: a pole is a rod or staff
IT is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A man called Rod retains a refined kind of sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined and well-mannered, as a person with good breeding and courtesy would be.

clue.text: Installed as bishop — on becoming all rapt?

indicators.note: one part becoming another means it is replaced by it

parts.note: a bishop is enthroned when formally installed in office

explanation.surface: A new bishop takes office and everyone is spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on becoming all' replaces the ON of ENTHRONED with ALL. The question mark flags 'rapt' as a loose sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellbound and captivated, held in complete fascination.

clue.text: Light grip needed on oar only after the start

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it
taking the word only from after its start means its first letter is lost

parts.note: a clamp is a device that grips

explanation.surface: A rower is told a firm grip is needed on the oar once the race has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective but is the noun definition; 'needed on' means placed after in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp is a powerful electric lamp, a kind of light source.

clue.text: Five lost to non-specific fever

indicators.note: lost to the word means removed from it

parts.note: vague means non-specific or imprecise
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A doctor gives up on five patients with a fever of unknown cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost to' removes V from VAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for malarial or shivering fits, a recurring feverish illness.

clue.text: Carping is fitting following constant promises to pay

indicators.note: the word for fitting follows the constant

parts.note: c is the physics symbol for the speed of light, a constant
apt means fitting or suitable
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Nagging complaints about debts seem appropriate after constant IOUs.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclined to find fault and raise petty objections, synonym of fault-finding.

clue.text: Curtailed intention to climb high mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so backwards
curtailed means having its tail, the last letter, cut off

parts.note: a plan is an intention

explanation.surface: Someone cuts short a plan to climb a lofty peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtailed' cuts PLAN to PLA; 'to climb' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lofty peak, especially in Switzerland, the source of the range named for them.

clue.text: Room is dangerous when son's going for run

indicators.note: the son's going in exchange for run means one letter swaps for the other

parts.note: parlous means perilous or dangerous
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A room becomes dangerous once the son runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'son's going for run' replaces the S in PARLOUS with R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting room in a private house, an old-fashioned word for a living space.

clue.text: Brilliant one among a set of diamonds

definitions.text: one among a set of diamonds
definitions.meaning: a single playing card from the diamond suit, the top one

explanation.surface: A jeweller admires one dazzling stone within a set of diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' looks like gems, but it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang praise for something excellent; also the single-pip card heading each suit in a pack.

clue.text: An indicator master and pupil are involved

indicators.note: letters that are involved get tangled together, signalling a rearrangement of the two words

explanation.surface: A teacher and a student are both involved in something, as if in a chemistry lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are involved' signals rearranging MASTER and PUPIL together.
explanation.definitionFit: This treated paper changes colour to show acidity or alkalinity, a classic chemical indicator used in school labs.

clue.text: Decline opportunity to go after drink

indicators.note: the word for opportunity is placed after the word for drink

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
your turn is your chance or opportunity

explanation.surface: Someone refuses the chance to follow a drink with another.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall or slump in activity or fortunes is a synonym for a decline.

clue.text: Note trouble about Kyoto's leader — this one?

definitions.text: Note trouble about Kyoto's leader — this one?

indicators.note: the note and the trouble go about, that is around, the next letter

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
ado is fuss or trouble

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A query whether a fuss over the ruler in Kyoto concerns this very figure.
explanation.walkthrough: MI and ADO go 'about' K, the first letter of Kyoto. The whole clue also describes the answer: Kyoto was the old imperial capital of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: The title once used abroad for the emperor of Japan, whose court sat at Kyoto.

clue.text: Brought up clear one in a normal style of presentation

indicators.note: the reversed word and one go in the following pieces

parts.note: usual means normal

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to void is to clear or empty
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A speaker raises a clear point in an ordinary manner of presenting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' reverses the word for clear; with one it goes 'in' the normal word, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Using both sound and images, a mode of presenting material in teaching or business.

clue.text: Minor British composer heard slips

indicators.note: heard means the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: petty means minor or trivial; Eric Coates was an English composer of light music

explanation.surface: A second-rate British composer is overheard making mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Coates wrote the Dam Busters March. 'slips' looks like errors but means undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: Underskirts worn beneath a dress, also called slips in women's clothing.

clue.text: City long ago installing king for English

indicators.note: installing one letter puts it into the word in place of another
for here means in place of, so one letter swaps out the other

parts.note: yore means times long past
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A city of long ago crowns a king in place of the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installing king for English' swaps the E of YORE for K. York is a historic city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: York is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire, England, an example of a city.

clue.text: Terrible din from low group of crows

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling low
a murder is the collective noun for crows

explanation.surface: A flock of crows makes a dreadful racket from somewhere down low.
explanation.walkthrough: To scream blue murder is a British idiom for making a loud outcry.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a loud, furious outcry, as in screaming at the top of your voice.

clue.text: Knock out length in terse revising for author

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout

indicators.note: the abbreviation for length goes in the rearranged word
revising a word changes it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor cuts some length from an author's terse prose while revising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revising' rearranges the word terse, and 'in' sets the length abbreviation inside it. Arthur Koestler wrote Darkness at Noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Koestler was a Hungarian-born British novelist and essayist, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Picture hotel suite when trashed

indicators.note: a trashed room is wrecked and messed up, signalling a rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A painting hangs in a hotel suite that guests have wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when trashed' rearranges HOTEL SUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark outline image against a light background is a kind of picture or portrait.

clue.text: Trouble a doctor's found up in African country

indicators.note: in a down clue, found up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
MO is a medical officer, so the doctor's gives MOS

explanation.surface: A doctor's troubles are discovered in an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found up' reverses AIL A MOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalia is a nation in the Horn of Africa, an example of an African state.

clue.text: Laments losing new flightless birds

indicators.note: losing a letter means it is dropped from the word

parts.note: moans are laments or complaints

explanation.surface: Lamenting creatures stop complaining about the new birds that cannot fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing new' takes N out of MOANS.
explanation.definitionFit: These were giant extinct ratites of New Zealand, unable to fly, like emus or kiwis.

clue.text: Second brew gets editor very drunk

parts.note: mash is the malt and water brewed for beer

explanation.surface: An editor who has a second brew ends up thoroughly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for heavily intoxicated, as if knocked to pieces by drink.

clue.text: Rook Maiden in Dorset follows?

definitions.meaning: the chess piece also known by this name
the word that follows Maiden to name the Iron Age hill fort in Dorset

explanation.surface: A rook in Dorset is pursued by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Maiden Castle is a huge Iron Age hill fort in Dorset, a county in south-west England. 'Maiden' looks like a girl but is the first word of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the piece is a rook; the word also completes the Dorset hill fort's name.

clue.text: Situation that's confusing men in crowd

indicators.note: the word for men goes in the word for crowd

parts.note: a mass is a large crowd
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers caught up in a crowd find things bewildering.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a bog: a complicated mess or entanglement one cannot get out of.

clue.text: Remain mostly around spies — a problem of nerves

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes around the spies
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to stick is to stay or remain
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Spies are told to stay put, a situation that is hard on the nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the word for remain, and 'around' wraps that round the US spy agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain running down the leg from a compressed sciatic nerve, a nerve disorder.

clue.text: Title of king associated with dynasty

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
the Han was an imperial Chinese dynasty

explanation.surface: A king's title is linked with his ruling dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank held by Mongol and Central Asian rulers, as in Genghis, so an honorific title.

clue.text: Confirmed single hotel nearly let go

indicators.note: letters let go are released from their order and fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A determined bachelor was almost thrown out of his hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let go' rearranges HOTEL NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone seeking love through personal ads, unattached; a confirmed single person.

clue.text: Some spirits meaning a chill in the air

definitions.meaning: a small measure of liquor, a dram
a sharp coldness, as in a frosty bite to the weather

explanation.surface: A drop of spirits is welcome when the air turns cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram of whisky; also the sharp, biting cold of a frosty morning.

clue.text: Plenty disregarding opera company? I don't like that at all

definitions.text: I don't like that at all

indicators.note: disregarding the company means leaving its letters out

parts.note: enough means plenty, a sufficient amount
ENO is English National Opera, a London company

explanation.surface: A disgruntled operagoer has had plenty of the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disregarding opera company' drops ENO from ENOUGH. English National Opera performs at the London Coliseum.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of disgust or distaste, the noise of strong dislike.

clue.text: Longing that's not good for easily available drug

indicators.note: the word that's not good has the abbreviation for good taken out

parts.note: aspiring means longing or striving for something

explanation.surface: A craving that is unhealthy for a drug anyone can get.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's not good' removes G from ASPIRING.
explanation.definitionFit: A common painkiller sold over the counter in any pharmacy, so freely obtainable medicine.

clue.text: Attacked poet failing to finish end of ballad

indicators.note: a word failing to finish loses its final letter

parts.note: Percy Bysshe Shelley was a Romantic poet

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A critic savaged a poet who could not complete his ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to finish' trims SHELLEY to SHELLE; 'end of ballad' adds D.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombarded with artillery shells, so attacked from a distance.
